'''Matsuzawa Yoshiakira''' (松沢 義章, 1791 - {{ill|1861|en|1861|qid=Q7693|lt=March 12, 1861|1=1861}}) was a late {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period|1=Edo period}} {{ill|Kokugaku|en|Kokugaku|qid=Q855159|lt=kokugaku|1=Kokugaku}} scholar. His common name was Shirōzaemon, and his pen names included Gako Sanjin and Shunju no Sha.

== Life ==
Born in {{ill|Shinano Province|en|Shinano Province|qid=Q289250|lt=Shimosuwa-shuku|1=Shinano Province}}, a post station in the {{ill|Suwa Region|lt=Suwa Region|lt=Suwa region|ja|諏訪地方|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa region|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 諏訪地域|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 諏訪地域}}, Matsuzawa was the son of Shirōzaemon, a merchant dealing in gold, silver, and tortoiseshell. The family shop, known as Maruya, had ancestral roots in the {{ill|Iida-jō|ja|飯田城 (信濃国)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iida-jō|1=Iida Castle|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11666503}} area, engaging in trade between {{ill|Edo|en|Edo|qid=Q215646|lt=Edo|1=Edo}}, Suwa, and Iida. Matsuzawa studied {{ill|Confucianism|en|Confucianism|qid=Q9581|lt=Confucianism|1=Confucianism}} under {{ill|Satō Issai|en|Satō Issai|qid=Q6463901|lt=Sato Issai|1=Satō Issai}}.

At the age of 43 in {{ill|Tenpō 4|ja|天保4年|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenpō 4|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (1833), Matsuzawa became a disciple of {{ill|Hirata Atsutane|en|Hirata Atsutane|qid=Q2572749|lt=Hirata Atsutane|1=Hirata Atsutane}}, delving into kokugaku. He demonstrated deep knowledge of the {{ill|Zuo Zhuan|en|Zuo Zhuan|qid=Q230230|lt=Spring and Autumn Annals|1=Zuo Zhuan}}, authoring *Shunju Taii* in {{ill|Tenpō 9|ja|天保9年|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenpō 9|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (1838), where he critiqued errors in {{ill|Du Yu|en|Du Yu|qid=Q702166|lt=Du Yu|1=Du Yu}}'s *Chunqiu Jingzhuan Jiji*. In Edo, he associated with figures such as {{ill|Takano Chōei|en|Takano Chōei|qid=Q944693|lt=Takano Chōei|1=Takano Chōei}}, {{ill|Mogami Tokunai|en|Mogami Tokunai|qid=Q4141812|lt=Mogami Tokunai|1=Mogami Tokunai}}, and {{ill|Hirata Kanetane|ja|平田銕胤|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirata Kanetane|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 平田鐵胤|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 平田鐵胤|1=Hirata Kanetane|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q6537446}}, while in Suwa, he maintained ties with {{ill|Iida Takekuni|ja|飯田武郷|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iida Takekuni|1=Iida Takesato|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q6535088}}. Matsuzawa was a proponent of imperial loyalty, becoming a foundational figure for kokugaku and imperial loyalist thought in the {{ill|Tenryū River|en|Tenryū River|qid=Q13667|lt=Tenryū River|1=Tenryū River}} region between Suwa and {{ill|Ina Valley|ja|伊那谷|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ina Valley|qq=}}.

Known for his versatility, Matsuzawa also studied {{ill|Korean language|en|Korean language|qid=Q9176|lt=Korean language|1=Korean language}}, composing Japanese waka in {{ill|Hangul|ja|諺文|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hangul|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ハングル|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ハングル|1=Hangul|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q8222}}. He designed a steam bath kettle that was confiscated by the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|1=Tokugawa shogunate|2=ja|3=江戸幕府|lt=Tokugawa shogunate|lt=Tokugawa Shogunate|ja|Tokugawa shogunate|1=Tokugawa shogunate|2=ja|3=江戸幕府|lt=Tokugawa shogunate|lt=Tokugawa Shogunate|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Shogunate|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. In his later years, Matsuzawa turned his attention to local history, researching topics related to the {{ill|Suwa-taisha|en|Suwa-taisha|qid=Q218813|lt=Suwa-taisha|1=Suwa-taisha}} and writing works such as *Suwa Kunikō*, *Suwa Koryōkō*, *Hōreishū*, and *Ken'yū Hongi*. He passed away in {{ill|Man'en 2|ja|万延2年|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Man'en 2|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 1861年|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 1861年|1=1861|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q7693}} (1861) and was buried at {{ill|Dizang Temple|en|Dizang Temple|qid=Q1231809|lt=Jizō-ji|1=Dizang Temple}}.
